column11: lookup.py demand Spinraza: CMS Medicare Part D 2020, $5,622,217.40 over 17 beneficiaries = $330,719 per beneficiary. This is the only Spinraza year with a beneficiary count; 2021-2024 are suppressed (under 11)
column12: Judgement on the comparator, as asked. Angelman syndrome has no marketed disease-modifying drug. Spinraza was chosen over Qalsody for four reasons: (1) SMA is also a paediatric-onset genetic neurological disease of similar rarity, treated in the same child-neurology centres. (2) Spinraza is also an Ionis-discovered intrathecal ASO. (3) Its maintenance dose comes every 4 months, against quarterly for obudanersen and every 28 days for Qalsody. (4) Qalsody's $108,202 per Part B beneficiary (2024) covers only 7.3 administrations of a monthly adult ALS drug, so it prices a partial year of a different disease. Four checks support the level. Spinraza's Part D cost per claim, one vial and one dose, was flat at $140,555 in 2020 and $141,108 in 2024, so the 2020 figure is not stale. The NY Medicaid DUR board (July 2020, health.ny.gov/health_care/medicaid/program/dur/meetings/2020/07/mdc_initiative.pdf, via search) gives a WAC of $382,500 for a maintenance year. Evrysdi, the oral SMA drug, reads $328,087 per Part D beneficiary in 2024 over 471 beneficiaries (lookup.py demand Evrysdi), within 1%. The case against: Spinraza is physician-administered and billed mainly under Part B (HCPCS J2326). The book carries no Spinraza Part B rows, so this is a 17-beneficiary minority channel. The figure also covers 2.35 doses per beneficiary, against 3 in a maintenance year, so it understates a full year: at the 2024 per-claim cost a maintenance year is about $423,000. Ionis sets its own price, and obudanersen's four doses a year could support a price above Spinraza's

The case for keeping it: Angelman patients rely heavily on Medicaid, which takes a statutory rebate of at least 23.1% plus inflation penalties. No product-level discount for Spinraza or an Angelman drug was found

column11: Gauthier-Loiselle M et al., 'Nusinersen for Spinal Muscular Atrophy in the United States: Findings From a Retrospective Claims Database Analysis', Adv Ther 2021;38(12):5809-5828 (PMID 34713391, doi:10.1007/s12325-021-01938-w): 12-month persistence of 55.2%, 42.4% and 54.6% in SMA types 1, 2 and 3 (23, 41 and 260 patients who completed loading). Weighted: (23 x 0.552 + 41 x 0.424 + 260 x 0.546) / 324 = 0.531, so 1 - 0.531 = 0.469
column12: Judgement: first-year persistence on Spinraza is applied as a constant annual rate. It is the same modality with the same lumbar-puncture burden, and the book has no measured persistence for an intrathecal paediatric drug. The case for lower: the study was funded by Novartis Gene Therapies, Zolgensma's maker. Zolgensma was approved inside the window (May 2019), so some stops were switches, and Angelman has no alternative therapy to switch to. Claims gaps also overstate stops: a Biogen study found 80.5-93.9% of doses given on time (Youn B et al., Adv Ther 2023, PMID 36645543). The case for higher: children with Angelman often need sedation for a lumbar puncture. The closest disease analogue is close to this value: Daybue, in Rett, had 45.1% of 1,175 initiators non-persistent (PMID 42287113)

Topline in late 2027 and an NDA in the first half of 2028 put approval in late 2028 on an 8-month priority review, which Breakthrough designation makes likely. 2029 is then the first full year. CHAMPION (NCT07782827, 30 participants, primary completion 2028-05) is a second, smaller Phase 3 that could also be wanted for the filing

column11: Birth incidence 1:24,580 (95% CI 1:23,727-1:25,433), genetically verified cases in the Danish national population (Mertz LGB et al., 'Angelman syndrome in Denmark. Birth incidence, genetic findings, and age at diagnosis', Am J Med Genet A 2013;161A(9):2197-2203, PMID 23913711, doi:10.1002/ajmg.a.36058) x US resident population of 340,110,988 on 1 July 2024 (US Census Bureau, Vintage 2024) = 13,837
column12: The book carries no Angelman pool (lookup.py pool Angelman returns nothing, and none is in epidemiology.csv), so this sets it. Judgement: a birth incidence times the living population assumes survival near that of the general population and a stable incidence across cohorts. The case for higher: the commonly quoted 1 in 12,000 to 20,000 gives 17,000 to 28,000. The case for lower: many older adults with Angelman were never diagnosed, and Estonia measured a point prevalence of 1:56,112 in children (PMID 16906556). The Danish rate counts diagnosed, genetically verified cases, so it sits near a diagnosed pool, which is the uptake anchor's basis. The Census figure was not re-checked by search in this session

column11: 3,596,017 US births in 2023 (NCHS, 'Births: Final Data for 2023', National Vital Statistics Reports 74(1), March 2025, PMID 40961109) / 24,580 (Mertz 2013, as above) = 146.3
column12: The same Danish birth incidence as the prevalence, so the two are consistent. Most cases are diagnosed at 21 to 46 months (Mertz 2013), so an affected birth enters the treatable pool with a lag the engine does not model

column11: REVEAL entry criterion: genetic confirmation of a UBE3A deletion or UBE3A mutation (Ionis release 2026-07-06, as above). Share of Angelman with those genotypes: 36 deletions + 4 UBE3A mutations of 51 genetically verified patients = 0.7843 (Mertz 2013, PMID 23913711, the same population as the pool; the others were 5 paternal UPD and 6 other)
column12: The label population is assumed to follow REVEAL's genotype criterion. No age filter is applied. REVEAL enrols ages 2 to 50, but under-2s are rarely diagnosed and a label may not cap age, as Spinraza's does not. That is a judgement. The case for lower: a label restricted to ages 2-50 excludes older adults. The case for higher: the mechanism, unsilencing the paternal UBE3A, also applies to UPD and imprinting-defect patients, who carry an intact paternal copy, and a later label could add them. The Danish sample is small (51)

column11: Solved from Daybue (trofinetide), the first drug approved for Rett syndrome (March 2023), a paediatric genetic neurodevelopmental disorder. It reached 987 unique US patients receiving a shipment in Q2 2025 and 954 in Q1 2025 (Acadia Q2 2025 results release, acadia.com/en-us/media/news-releases/acadia-pharmaceuticals-reports-second-quarter-2025-financial). Through the engine's own functions (backend/forecast.py derive_new_patients and treated_stock) with Daybue's inputs: US pool 7,500, the midpoint of Acadia's 6,000 to 9,000 US Rett patients (as reported by Fierce Pharma, fiercepharma.com/pharma/acadia-seeks-chmp-re-examination-rett-syndrome-med-daybue-following-eu-rejection); the book's Vyvgart curve (k 0.5633, midpoint 2.0) with 2023 as year 0; and discontinuation 0.451 (45.1% of 1,175 initiators non-persistent, Rashid N et al., J Med Econ 2026;29(1):1715-1727, PMID 42287113, doi:10.1080/13696998.2026.2682668). A stock of 987 in 2025 gives a peak of 0.1856 (0.1523 at 9,000, 0.2379 at 6,000)
column12: Judgement: the multiple over Daybue is 1.0. Cross-check: 290 of 1,820 US adults with Rett in claims (15.9%) started trofinetide in its first year (Rashid N et al., Front Neurol 2026, PMID 42577214, doi:10.3389/fneur.2026.1856312). The case for lower: a lumbar puncture every quarter, often under sedation in Angelman, is a larger barrier than an oral solution. The pool here counts adults never genetically confirmed, and Ionis is a first-time rare-disease launcher. The case for higher: Daybue's GI intolerance held it back, and Angelman families are organised and trial-ready (FAST, ASF). A communication benefit shown on Bayley-4 would be the first disease-modifying result. Solved with the modeled pool at 1.0 carryover and no Rett incidence, a small simplification over 3 years
